CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Manggarai Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Manggarai.
4. Implementation of Protection of women and children is the process, method, act of implementing protection for women and children.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence is any form of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering that is physical, emotional/psychological, economic, sexual and social to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any form of action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
10. Victim is a woman including Female Workers and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such violence.
11. Protection of women is all acts aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are to: a. prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children; b. accompany women and children victims of violence in legal processes both litigation and non-litigation in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
c. provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence; and
d. restore the physical and psychological condition of women and children victims of violence.

1.9.rationale: In the Indonesian source, Pasal 4 explicitly includes "eksploitasi" (Art. 4 huruf f) and "perdagangan perempuan dan anak" (huruf g). The Penjelasan Pasal 4 huruf f further defines exploitation as forcing women/children to do something without regard to their development (a broad exploitation concept). While the text does not explicitly say "sexual slavery" by name, the indicator is "Sexual slavery / exploitation" and the regulation clearly covers exploitation as a form of violence, alongside sexual violence and trafficking. The retrieved English candidates included both Art. 4 (listing exploitation) and the elucidation defining exploitation, so a judge could reasonably answer Yes for exploitation coverage. The judge was overly strict by requiring explicit mention of sexual exploitation/sexual slavery as a distinct subcategory despite the policy’s explicit inclusion of exploitation and trafficking.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF MANGGARAI REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2018
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Efforts to implement protection for women and children must continue to be carried out and the implementation should be conducted in a coordinated and integrated manner among related agencies and/or bodies. To support the smooth implementation of the protection for women and children in Manggarai Regency, a regional regulation is needed that regulates the protection of women and children.
In order to support such implementation, it is necessary to regulate the mechanisms and cooperation starting from the recovery of victims in terms of their physical and/or psychological condition, by determining the duties and functions of each party and the obligations and responsibilities of health workers, spiritual counselors and volunteer companions. To make integrated services more effective, this regional regulation establishes a mechanism that will coordinate among service officers, while simultaneously formulating program plans for improving efforts to implement protection for women and children.
Cooperation in implementing protection for women and children is directed toward prevention, handling and restoration of the victims' condition to their original state both physically and psychologically within a not too lengthy period of time, so that victims can carry out their daily activities and can live in the community as before. Therefore, services must be implemented as maximally as possible immediately after there is a complaint or report from victims to obtain services for the recovery of the condition of women and children victims of violence. In addition, efforts to eliminate violence preventively are also continuously carried out in various ways, so that violence against women and children in the long term can be eliminated or at minimum its numbers can be reduced.

Article 8
(1) Regional Government in the implementation of protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 6
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. providing education on anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. collecting data and information on Women and Children Victims of Violence; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention, handling, recovery and rehabilitation efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the duties of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

2.1.rationale: The Indonesian regulation establishes internal coordination/integration mechanisms within the Manggarai Regency system (e.g., Penjelasan Umum: "terkoordinasi dan terpadu antar dinas dan/atau badan yang terkait"; Pasal 9(3): monitoring via "koordinasi" with institutions/work units; Pasal 7: Integrated Service Center accommodating various units). However, it does not describe an institutional network across jurisdictions (other regencies/provinces/national government) or an inter-governmental coordination framework. The judge’s rationale matches the Indonesian text: coordination is intra-daerah among agencies/bodies, not an inter-jurisdictional network. Therefore the golden label 'Yes' appears incorrect for an indicator framed as an institutional network/coordination mechanism beyond a single local government.

Therefore, services must be implemented as maximally as possible immediately after there is a complaint or report from victims to obtain services for the recovery of the condition of women and children victims of violence. In addition, efforts to eliminate violence preventively are also continuously carried out in various ways, so that violence against women and children in the long term can be eliminated or at minimum its numbers can be reduced.

(1) Regional Government in the implementation of protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Manggarai Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Manggarai.
4. Implementation of Protection of women and children is the process, method, act of implementing protection for women and children.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence is any form of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering that is physical, emotional/psychological, economic, sexual and social to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any form of action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
10. Victim is a woman including Female Workers and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such violence.
11. Protection of women is all acts aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.

(1) Regional apparatus that carries out the function of empowerment and protection of women and children shall conduct monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures and implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence.

FUNDING
Article 12
Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other legitimate and non-binding sources of financing.

Because the most relevant phrasing supporting the golden 'Yes' was not surfaced to the judge, retrieval likely failed for this indicator.

CHAPTER V
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 6
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention, handling and recovery efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. providing education on anti-violence values towards women and children;
c. collecting data and information on Women and Children Victims of Violence; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention, handling, recovery and rehabilitation efforts for victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.
